title: cross-pool-latency-cap-and-spillover-hedger
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduce cross-pool burst capping allocator that respects per-pool tail-latency budgets and emits new telemetry for capped spillover events. Config behind feature flag. Backwards-compatible; default off.
commits: init: cross-pool allocator core and interfaces
feat: hedger reconciler and smoothing factor controller
test: unit tests for allocator and hedger (latency, headroom scenarios)
telemetry: add crosspool_burst_capped_total and pool_headroom_estimate metrics
docs: ops playbook and config examples
fix: tighten concurrency path and address race in allocator cache
description: Context: Customers with dedicated fleets were observing tail latency spikes when one busy tenant spilled load into adjacent pools. Existing soft-burst mechanisms allowed spillover but had no cross-pool latency budget enforcement, which could push under-provisioned pools past their SLOs. Motivation: introduce a policy-driven allocator that proactively caps inter-pool spillover when the downstream pool's tail latency budget is endangered, and report capped events so SRE and capacity ops can observe and act. Summary: this PR implements a cross-pool latency-capped spillover allocator + a hedger (reconciler) that smooths commit ramps and updates per-pool hedging factor based on sampled headroom and observed latency percentiles. The feature is behind feature flag `crosspool_capping`. Changes include: - allocator core + interfaces (pkg/autoscaler) - reconciler loop that adjusts smoothing/hedge on a control interval - telemetry hooks (new metrics and labels) - e2e integration test that simulates spillover and asserts tail-latency stays within configured budget - docs and ops playbook entries - helm values for dedicated fleets Feature checklist: [x] design doc (Linear: ENG-2148) linked [x] unit tests added [x] e2e integration added [x] telemetry names reviewed [x] config flag gated and defaulted to false Backwards compatibility and rollout: default is off; rollout plan in docs recommends progressive enablement per pool with small hedging factor and monitoring on `crosspool_burst_capped_total` and `pool_headroom_estimate`. On failure modes the allocator falls back to existing soft-burst behavior (conservative path) to avoid hard rejects. CI: initial run failed a flakey e2e (timing); rerun passed. Performance: microbenchmarks show allocator adds ~0.5% CPU on autoscaler controller and latency-sensitive path unchanged in non-capping mode. Limitations: current headroom estimate uses short-window percentile and can be noisy for very low QPS pools; we map a minimum-sample floor and avoid enforcing strict caps below that threshold. Related: ENG-2148 (design), small follow-up planned to add per-tenant opt-out and more sophisticated forecasting for headroom. Merge: squash-merged after approvals and CI green.
